p7:main.evidence: reports/task6-summary-evidence/academic/dated-controller-comparison/0914.json question p7, subpart main; frozen dated-group1/results.json; root-adjudication.json. Derivative roots -2±sqrt(5) and second derivative signs ±6sqrt(5) agree, as do heights 17∓10sqrt(5). Both limit these to local extrema and find no stationary saddle.
p7:main.conclusion: Local maximum (-2-sqrt(5),17+10sqrt(5)); local minimum (-2+sqrt(5),17-10sqrt(5)); no stationary saddle point.
derivation: f prime=3x^2+12x-3=3((x+2)^2-5). Thus stationary x=-2-sqrt(5) and -2+sqrt(5).
f double prime=6x+12. At the first root it is -6sqrt(5)<0 (strict local maximum); at the second it is +6sqrt(5)>0 (strict local minimum).
Writing t=x+2 gives f=t^3-15t+17; t=±sqrt(5) gives heights 17∓10sqrt(5).
checks: Derivative vanishes exactly at both roots.
Both second derivatives nonzero. These are local extrema; a cubic is unbounded in both directions.
p7:main.comparison_condition: Derivative roots -2±sqrt(5) and second derivative signs ±6sqrt(5) agree, as do heights 17∓10sqrt(5). Both limit these to local extrema and find no stationary saddle.
